title: Partnerships and location agreements
audience: Owners who work with complementary businesses or train at venues other than their own
learningOutcomes: Score potential partner businesses against stated fit criteria
Describe what a written partnership note and a venue agreement should cover
Identify the referral payment, insurance and workplace points that have not yet been confirmed and need advice

instruction.heading: Partner with businesses that already serve your clients
instruction.body: The best partner already serves people like your ideal client, has a sound reputation, and is close to your service area. Depending on the area, candidates include allied health and wellness businesses, retailers of sports or nutrition products, and early-childhood providers. Score each candidate on client overlap, reputation, distance and whether you already have a relationship. Avoid businesses that compete for the same clients with the same service.

instruction.heading: Make the partnership mutual and in writing
instruction.body: A partnership works when both sides gain something useful, such as a joint talk, a free assessment for the partner's staff, or a shared article. Put the arrangement in a one-page note: what each side provides, how referrals are passed on, how client information is shared, and how either side may end it. Any referral payment is a separate decision. It must be disclosed, recorded in writing, and checked for legal and professional-conduct issues before use. Cash payments for referrals are not assumed in this lesson.

instruction.heading: Location agreements set the terms
instruction.body: Training at a private gym, studio or a client's home is a commercial arrangement. The written agreement should state the revenue split, who pays for insurance and cleaning, access and cancellation terms, who holds client records, and what happens if the venue closes. The percentage a venue accepts is a negotiation, not a standard.

procedure: Name five businesses already reaching your ideal client. Rate each from 1 to 5 on client overlap, reputation, distance and existing relationship.
Choose the highest scorer and draft a one-page partnership note.
If any payment is proposed, write it down, disclose it where relevant, and get advice before agreeing.
For a venue or home-visit arrangement, draft written terms covering the points in the instruction.
Review the arrangement at 90 days against agreed measures.

workedExamples.situation: A hypothetical yoga teacher is offered a room at a physiotherapy clinic for a fixed weekly fee plus a share of referrals.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must be settled in writing before the first class?
workedExamples.reasoning: The room fee, the referral arrangement, insurance, access hours, client records, and what happens if the clinic changes its services all need writing. Any referral payment must be disclosed and checked before it is agreed.

commonErrors.prevention: Put every term in writing and have both sides sign.

commonErrors.error: Offering unlimited free sessions to a partner's staff
commonErrors.prevention: Set a fixed number of free places with an end date.
Disclose and record any payment, and get advice before agreeing it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Get advice on disclosure, professional-conduct and consumer law obligations before agreeing any referral payment.
Check the insurer's terms in writing for insurance responsibilities under a venue or home-visit agreement.
This lesson does not grant a venue's approval to train on its premises, and does not confirm any state or territory workplace duty for home visits.

qualityStandard: Each partner has a recorded score and reason
Every partnership and venue arrangement is in writing and signed
Each payment point is disclosed, and no payment is agreed until advice is obtained
documentationEvidence: Signed partnership note or venue agreement
Referral and payment register where any payment exists
summary: Partner with businesses that already reach your clients.
Put every partnership and venue term in writing.

knowledgeChecks.question: A strong partner for a fitness business is most likely a business that:
options: Competes with you for the same clients and charges less than you do
Already serves your target clients and has a good reputation
Has no clients and no website and has no social media page

knowledgeChecks.question: Before any referral payment is agreed, the lesson requires:
options: A verbal agreement only, made over a coffee in the gym
Written terms, disclosure, and advice on the legal position
Payment in cash so that no records exist and no tax is declared

knowledgeChecks.question: A venue agreement should set out:
options: The trainer's favourite exercises and the music played in each class
The revenue split, access, insurance responsibility and who holds records
Only the venue's opening hours and the car park and the parking fees
